title: Swallowed kerosene, petrol, or paraffin (hydrocarbon)
summary: Kerosene, petrol, lamp oil, and paint thinners are 'hydrocarbons'. The main danger is not the stomach — it is the lung damage if any is breathed in. Vomiting must NOT be induced.
steps: Move the person to fresh air, away from any fumes.
Wipe any liquid from the mouth, face, and clothes. Remove and isolate any contaminated clothing.
Keep the person sitting upright or lying on their side. Do not lay them flat on their back.
Rinse the mouth with clean water and spit it out — do not swallow.
Note how much was swallowed, when, and which product (bring the container if safe).
Call emergency or a poison control line immediately and follow their instructions.
If they become unresponsive, place in the recovery position and monitor breathing while help arrives.
avoid: Do NOT make the person vomit. Hydrocarbons aspirated into the lungs cause severe chemical pneumonia.
Do not give milk, oil, or 'home antidotes'.
Do not give activated charcoal unless instructed by medical staff.
Do not give food or drink while waiting for help, except a small mouth rinse spat out.
whenToEscalate: Always emergency — every kerosene or hydrocarbon ingestion needs a hospital review.
Especially urgent if: coughing, choking, gagging, wheezing, breathlessness, hoarse voice, drowsiness, confusion, or seizures.
Any infant or small child who has swallowed any amount — emergency immediately.
Skin or eye contact along with ingestion — irrigate copiously and get to hospital.
specialty: Emergency department; involve a poison control centre if available.
